description:
This ticket stands up runtime-demand facts behind the existing seal barrier without moving authority away from the monolith yet. The fear is not that the fact path prints the same internal trace as `settle_runtime_demands`; the fear is that the agenda path can hide missing dependencies, global scans, or dropped executable demand facts while appearing to work.

## Goal
Stand up the first correct-by-construction fact shape for runtime demand:

- `ReturnDemand(E)` is a contribution-joined fact: entry needs, caller observed return use, and callable-boundary return evidence all join into the callee result demand.
- `RuntimeDemand(E)` is the derived executable demand fact: return demand, input demands, value demands, entry-capture demands, call-arg demands, and callable flows for one executable.
- `DeriveRuntimeDemand(E)` is an agenda job whose dependencies are explicit facts. The agenda, not a whole-closure inner loop, becomes the fixpoint driver.

## What We Learned
The original proposal is right for direct calls: `RuntimeDemand(E)` can be derived from facts for `E`, `ReturnDemand(E)`, and the specific `RuntimeDemand(callee)` facts for E local call targets. Self-recursion is still local: when `E` reads its own previous runtime-demand fact, the fresh `ReturnDemand(E)` must win for this firing.

Captured local callables need an explicit reverse/indexed relation. The old monolith hides this as a full scan over `all_demands`; the fact path must model it as data keyed by producer identity and capture prefix/surface. Do not recreate the monolith with `RuntimeDemandInventory(root)`, `runtime_demand_keys()`, or any other global scan of all runtime-demand facts.

## Change
1. Add `FactKey::ReturnDemand(ExecutableKey)` as a cumulative/contribution-joined fact beside `ReturnType` and `ActivationInputs`.
2. Add `FactKey::RuntimeDemand(ExecutableKey)` as an overwrite fact backed by a `RuntimeDemandMap` store.
3. Add `JobEffects.return_demand_contributions` and world wiring that mirrors activation-input contribution conclude/extend behavior. Normalize demands at the contribution/store seam.
4. Add `Job::DeriveRuntimeDemand(ExecutableKey)` and dispatch. It may read only the facts needed for that executable transfer: executable presence, settled activation/body/callsite facts, `ReturnDemand(E)`, specific neighbor runtime-demand facts, and explicit captured-callable back-link facts introduced by this ticket.
5. Re-express `base_return_demand` as contributions: the root seed contributes entry need, callers contribute observed delivered-result use, and callable-boundary evidence contributes boundary return demand. There is no global `locally_called` prepass in the fact path.
6. Keep the seal in shadow mode: for every discovered executable, enqueue/wait for `RuntimeDemand(E)` and assert the shadow facts are complete and well-formed for that executable frontier. The seal still uses monolith runtime demand as the authoritative output.

## Non-Negotiables
- No guessed helper paths left behind. If an attempted model does not pass, remove it before trying the next one.
- No `RuntimeDemandInventory`, no root-wide runtime-demand key iteration, and no global locally-called reconstruction in the new fact path.
- If captured-callable propagation needs a relationship the current facts cannot express, add the relationship as a first-class fact/index or split the ticket with a new blocking ticket. Do not hide it in scans.
- Do not force byte-for-byte equality between the fact path and monolith internal `ExecutableRuntimeDemand` maps. Internal value/call-arg provenance can differ. The later cutover needs equivalence at the transport projection boundary, not trace identity.

## Why
The agenda should compute runtime-demand facts through explicit dependencies. Direct calls already fit that shape. Captured local callables reveal the missing back-link relation; modeling it explicitly is the difference between incrementalizing the compiler and moving the old full pass into a new container.

## Rip Out
Nothing production-facing yet. The monolith remains authoritative until the shadow path is proven at the consumer boundary.

Any temporary scaffolding added while discovering the correct fact shape must either be removed before commit or tracked by a follow-up ticket that explicitly says when and why it goes away.

## Check
The seal waits for one settled `RuntimeDemand(E)` fact per executable in the monolith frontier and verifies those facts are structurally complete for that frontier. Run the focused runtime-demand tests that cover recursion, first-class callables, direct returned callables, transport callable surfaces, and reducer/suspend-continuation capture. Then run the agreed compiler2/fixture corpus. Zero warnings.
title: Runtime demand: stand up DeriveRuntimeDemand(E) facts behind the seal barrier in shadow mode
